examples.input: `config set model opus --reason no-op` (as human:owner; model is already `opus`)

results.1: exit 0, no output; the file is untouched (all four arms)
results.2: exit 0, no output; the file is untouched (both arms)

examples.input: `config set name coder` (as agent:bot; the file has `name: "coder"`, quoted)

results.1: exit 0, no output; the file is untouched and its quotes and comment are kept (all four arms)
results.2: exit 0, no output; the file is untouched and its quotes and comment are kept (both arms)

examples.input: `config set temperature 0.20` (as agent:bot; the file has `temperature: 0.2`)

results.1: exit 0, no output; 0.20 is treated as the same value and the file is untouched (all four arms)
results.2: exit 0, no output; 0.20 is treated as the same value and the file is untouched (both arms)

results.1: exit 0; 5 entries. Entries 1–4 are `import` records of the starting values (actor unknown). Entry 5 is `set retries 3 -> 4` by human:owner with the reason "real change". The three no-op commands left no entry: no "no-op" reason, and nothing from agent:bot (all four arms)
results.2: exit 0; 5 entries. Entries 1–4 are `import` records of the starting values (actor unknown). Entry 5 is `set retries 3 -> 4` by human:owner with the reason "real change". The three no-op commands left no entry: no "no-op" reason, and nothing from agent:bot (both arms)

context.in_practice: There is no visible difference between the routes. Every arm on both routes skipped saving and logging for the no-op commands. Only the timestamps and change IDs in the history differ.
context.stakes: When someone sets a config key to the value it already has, should the tool leave the file and the history alone, or rewrite the file and log a change that changed nothing? If it logs one, the audit trail fills up with fake changes credited to whoever ran the command. If it rewrites the file, the hand-written comments and quoting are at risk.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 makes 'no change, no save, no history entry' a deliberate rule. Route 2 did not consider the case, yet behaved the same in this run, so the behavior depends on nothing in its design keeping it that way.

plan_why: Shows whether a `set` that changes no value still rewrites the file (for example re-quoting or reformatting it) or records history events, including the edge cases of an equal value in another spelling and a `--reason` given with an unchanged value, compared with a real change.
routes: Save and stamp nothing when there are no events
